validation.note: 'per' is a binary operator, so its whole right-hand group is the divisor: (ng/mL)/(mg/kg) = ng·kg/(mL·mg). kg belongs in the numerator. Flattening 'per' to '/' gave ng/(kg·mL·mg), i.e. mass^-1 instead of mass^+1 -- wrong by kg^2. Scale stays 1.0 because ng·kg/mg cancels exactly, so the defect was invisible in the value and only detectable in the dimension.

CYP2D6 is an enzyme designator, not a unit with an exponent. The bare-exponent rule rewrote it to CYP^2·d6 -- inventing a squared dimension on an unresolvable token -- and the casing pass lowercased the D. That part of the invariant is unchanged: the designator must survive as one intact token. RE-VALIDATED 2026-08-05: the expected status moved from cleaned_only_unrecognized_unit to folded_pair because CYP2D6 is now a declared qualifier for this task. That is a deliberate decision, not drift: pmol CYP2D6 is a genuine enzyme-amount basis, the dimension (amount:-1, time:-1, volume:1) was already correct while quarantined, and the designator stays in the canonical key so CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 remain separate pair buckets. Declaring CYP alone as vocabulary re-broke the split (CYP^2·D6) until _bare_exponent was taught to prefer the longest declared token.

A mean and its variation may legitimately carry different exponents; 2.470e-5 = 0.0000247 and 5.327e-7 = 0.0000005327 both read literally off the source text. These were previously rejected as ambiguous_scientific_notation purely because the two factors differed, which quarantined real Caco-2 permeability measurements. The unit factor is dropped (set to None) when the two differ, since no single factor describes the pair.

mg^(2/3) is a fractional power the integer-exponent engine cannot represent. It previously folded to mL/h·mg by silently discarding the (2/3), producing a confidently wrong dimension. Failing closed is the only correct outcome: an unrepresentable exponent must leave the unit unrecognized rather than be approximated.

'skin' is skin_reaction vocabulary and occurs in zero bioavailability records. While the qualifier set was global, declaring it dimensionless for skin also declared it dimensionless for bioavailability, silently promoting records out of quarantine in a task that never uses the token. Under bioavailability's vocabulary it must stay unresolved. The companion case asserts the same string does resolve for skin_reaction.

The same unit string that must stay unresolved for bioavailability must resolve for skin_reaction, which declares 'skin'. This pair is the point of the task-scoped vocabulary: one task's parsing can no longer be changed by another task's declarations.

A shared qualifier must still take a bare exponent: 'mg protein-1' is the standard intrinsic-clearance basis. Gating exponent promotion on _BASE_UNITS alone left 'protein-1' unpromoted, so the token stayed unresolved and 138 real records fell out of folding. _is_known_unit_token therefore consults the declared qualifier vocabulary. The dimension is now asserted: mass is negative because the '-1' applies to the whole 'mg protein' basis, which _bind_compound_basis now enforces so this form agrees with the slash spelling.

The four real spellings of intrinsic clearance -- 'µL/min/mg protein', 'µL·min^-1·mg protein^-1', 'µL min-1 mg protein-1' and 'µL/(min·mg protein)' -- must produce one canonical key and one dimension. The exponent spellings previously gave mass:+1 because '^-1' bound to 'protein' alone, so the same quantity landed in a different pair bucket with an inverted mass basis and a scale wrong by 10^6. 'per mg protein' inverts the whole basis.

For a compound percent unit, stripping only the '%' leaves the rest of the unit stranded in the measurement ('5% per hour' -> '5 per hour'), which no longer parses and destroys the scalar. The whole-suffix strip already handles this correctly, so the percent branch yields to it when its own result does not parse -- but only when the fallback actually recovers a scalar, so non-scalar percent text keeps its existing rendering.

A bare integer in a denominator is a basis count: mL/100 g is per hundred grams, so 2.4 becomes 0.024 mL/g. The parser previously dropped the 100 entirely and folded to mL/g unchanged -- confidently 100x high, with no unknown token to flag it. Cerebral blood flow is the clearest reader of this basis: physiological CBF is ~50 mL/100 g/min, which stored against mL/g would read as 50 mL/g/min. BBB alone patched this per-task; bio and skin were simply wrong.

4.61 mg per 24 hours is 4.61/24 = 0.1920833... mg/h. Non-100 integers were left as unresolved tokens, quarantining the record; only the literal 100 was special-cased, and that one was dropped rather than folded.

week is an unambiguous time unit (7 d = 604800 s) that was simply absent from the base table, so µg/cm^2/week lost its time dimension and read as an areic dose rather than a flux. The value is unchanged because wk is its own canonical unit; what matters is that time:-1 is present so it cannot pool with µg/cm^2.

The casing table mapped the plurals (moles, mmoles, µmoles) but not the prefixed singulars, so mmole stayed unresolved and the unit resolved to dimension {volume:-1} alone -- the amount dimension was silently lost rather than flagged, which is the dangerous shape. Pure spelling: the value does not move.

'percent' spelled out is '%', the same class of spelling normalization as hr->h and liter->L. The two-word 'per cent' was worse than unrecognized: the 'per' operator split it into '/cent'. Joining it before the per rewrite is why that case is fixed too.

DELIBERATE NON-SUPPORT -- do not 'fix' this. Arbitrary units are by definition not comparable across studies: one paper's AU has no relation to another's. Declaring AU dimensionless would let two unrelated arbitrary scales fold into one canonical key and share a pair bucket, inventing a comparison that does not exist. Staying unrecognized makes the record non-scalar and so ineligible for pair buckets and assay transfer, which is the correct outcome. Same reasoning covers a.u., SI and score.

DELIBERATE NON-SUPPORT -- do not 'fix' this. A score is ordinal, not a ratio scale: differences and ratios between scores are not meaningful, so it must not become a dimensionless number that the distance geometry can operate on. Ordinal outcomes belong to the categorical encoder path, which assigns a declared scale, not to the unit parser.

'cells' is a genuine count base unit and 'million' is a multiplier on that basis, exactly like the 10^6 spelling which already folded. The two spellings of one quantity previously disagreed in BOTH value (5 vs 5e-6 for the same CLint) and canonical key ('µL/cells·min' vs 'µL/cells·million·min'), so identical measurements landed in different pair buckets. Numeric words must fold into scale, never become dimensionless qualifiers: a qualifier would leave the value 10^6 wrong while making the unit look resolved. 2.65/1e6 = 2.65e-6.

'sq.cm' is cm^2. Left alone it parsed one power short -- µg/sq.cm resolved to length:-1, an areic dose read as a linear density -- so the dimension was wrong, not merely unresolved. It only failed closed because 'sq' itself was unknown, which means declaring 'sq' a qualifier would have made it silently wrong. Fixed as a spelling rewrite alongside hr->h, covering sq/cu with or without periods and spaces.

Organ names are the same class as the already-declared brain and tissue: the dimension parses correctly and only the unresolved name blocks folding. The value does not move. 'liver' stays in the canonical key, so mL/min/g liver and mL/min/g kidney remain separate pair buckets rather than pooling into mL/min/g.

'equiv' here means parent-drug equivalents of a radiolabel -- a dimensionless basis note on an otherwise complete unit (ng per cm^2). Distinct from mEq, the milliequivalent, which is a single token and therefore untouched by declaring the standalone word; see the companion mEq case.

DELIBERATE NON-SUPPORT -- do not 'fix' this. A milliequivalent is an amount scaled by ionic charge, which we do not model as a dimension; folding it would require a valence we do not have. It is deliberately NOT reached by declaring 'eq'/'equiv' as qualifiers, because mEq is a single token rather than a prefix plus the standalone word. This case exists to pin that separation: if a future change makes mEq resolve, the equivalents vocabulary has leaked into a real unit.

'times' is the word form of 'fold', which is already a base unit -- the same spelling class as hr->h. 'increase'/'decrease'/'reduction' become qualifiers so 'fold increase' resolves, and because qualifiers stay in the canonical key a fold-increase ('fold·increase') can never pool with a fold-decrease ('fold·decrease'). Status is cleaned_pair rather than folded_pair because clean_unit already rewrites 'times' to 'fold', so the canonical and cleaned units agree and nothing needs folding.

The dalton (unified atomic mass unit) is a real mass unit, 1 Da = 1.66053906660e-27 kg, and was simply absent from the base table so molecular weights carried no dimension at all. 106 Da is a plausible small-molecule mass. Low volume and molecular weight is unlikely to participate in assay transfer, but a real unit costs one table entry and leaving it out means a genuine mass reads as dimensionless.

The real Fa source and support sentence both contain 40-70,50, so there is no independent evidence that the final comma means a 70.50 endpoint rather than damaged list or table punctuation. Stage 01 must preserve the authoritative display form, and a bypassed Stage-02 parser must fail closed instead of inventing a scalar range.
